acceptance: A test shows one timeout followed by success yields the normal gate result, not an error.
A test shows exhausted retries still post failure, with a status naming the request kind in <= 140 chars and no 'to failed' gap.
Shipped in a Theseus release and the BenchBox lock promoted; links recorded.
context: Found while landing BenchBox #4172 (Theseus v0.2.11 lock). Gate run 43254778156, job 131315580586.
description:
Observed on BenchBox #4172 (head e7617006, 2026-11-12T16:10Z): review-gate posted `failure` with `Gate error · GitHub request to failed: <urlopen error timed out> · see the run log`. The gate job then ended `cancelled`, so the BenchBox `gate posting check` failed ('the gate job ended cancelled') although the next three gate runs posted `Pass · review-verdict: SHIP`. Recovery needed a manual re-run of the failed jobs.
Two defects:
1. No retry on a transient network error. review_check.py:320,468,487 and gate.py:128 raise CheckError on the first urlopen failure. github.py already has a retry/backoff path (`from .retry import State`); the gate's reads do not use it.
2. The posted status text loses the URL. The source is f"GitHub request to {url} failed: {exc}", but the shortened status reads 'GitHub request to failed', which leaves a reader with no endpoint. The status shortener presumably strips the URL and leaves broken grammar.
Fix: retry idempotent GET reads on timeouts, connection resets and 5xx with bounded backoff inside the job time budget; keep posting failure (fail closed) when the retries are exhausted. Make the shortened status name the request kind (for example 'reading PR reviews') instead of a URL.
Guardrails: an unreadable state must never post success; no retry on 4xx other than 429/403 rate limit with Retry-After; tests with a fake transport for timeout-then-success and timeout-exhausted; status text stays <= 140 chars; G7 merge rule plus independent review (gate change).
